issue: Does a hotel guest keep a reasonable expectation of privacy in a room after checkout time, such that a grace period applies when the hotel's pattern or practice or its communications with the guest make the late stay reasonable?

sides.position: A guest may retain a legitimate expectation of privacy after checkout time if the hotel has a pattern or practice that makes the expectation reasonable.
cases: United States v. Kitchens, 114 F.3d 29, 32 (4th Cir. 1997)
United States v. Owens, 782 F.2d 146, 150 (10th Cir. 1986)
United States v. Lanier, 636 F.3d at 232 (circuit not named in excerpt)
United States v. Dorais, 241 F.3d at 1129 (circuit not named in excerpt)

sides.position: No post-checkout exception applies; the Fourth Amendment expectation of privacy ends under clear rules, rejecting a hotel-practice-based grace period.
cases: United States v. Ross, 964 F.3d at 1043 n.6 (circuit not named in excerpt)

quote: Circuits disagree on these questions, and we need not weigh in here.
cite: United States v. Ryan Mendoza, No. 25-1154 (3rd Cir. 2026)
